area: examples/ acceptance suite (both arms, both modes), sandbox three-arm parity, benchmarks evidence policy + hash integrity + perf-claim reproduction, root package.json scripts, npm pack contents
claim: The three sandbox arms are not behaviorally equivalent outside the four claimed happy/domain-error paths, contradicting sandbox/README.md's "expose the same create/get notes behavior": the Express arm answers invalid input with 500 + an HTML ZodError stack trace (leaked to the client) where the Agentix arm returns 400 {ok:false,error:{code:"INVALID_INPUT",issues}}; wrong method is 404 (Express) vs 405+Allow (Agentix); malformed percent-encoding is 400 HTML (Express) vs 404 JSON (Agentix); and the NestJS arm cannot serve HTTP at all (package.json ships only @nestjs/common — no @nestjs/core or platform adapter) and its controller returns ok:false envelopes with no status mapping and throws raw ZodError on invalid input. Happy/domain paths (201/409/200/404 with identical JSON envelopes) DO match, so the SPEC §5 scoped claim holds; the divergence is a comparability caveat for the full-src "≤ Express arm" token evidence (the Express arm implements strictly less error behavior — direction is conservative for Agentix, so the headline still stands).
repro: Booted both HTTP-capable arms from dist and diffed a 12-request matrix (script since removed per instructions; it imported sandbox/notes-app/dist/app.js via handler.fetch and sandbox/plain-notes-app/dist/app.js on a real node:http server, plus nestjs-notes-app controller directly). Observed: POST /notes {id,title:"  ",body} → agentix 400 {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_INPUT",...}} vs express 500 "<!DOCTYPE html>...ZodError: [...] at NotesService.create (.../notes-service.js:5:43)..."; extra-key and missing-field inputs likewise 400-JSON vs 500-HTML; PUT /notes → 405 vs 404; GET /notes/%E0%A4%A → 404 JSON vs 400 HTML URIError page; NestJS controller.create({title:"  "}) throws ZodError, duplicate create returns {ok:false,...} with no HTTP status semantics, and NestFactory cannot be used (no @nestjs/core in sandbox/nestjs-notes-app/package.json). Happy/domain rows (create 201, dup 409, get 200, missing 404) matched byte-comparable envelopes across arms.
suggestedFix: Either scope the sandbox/README.md parity claim explicitly to the tested envelope (create 201/409, get 200/404 — dispatch/service level for NestJS), or add a small Express error middleware mapping ZodError→400 {ok:false,error:{code:"INVALID_INPUT",issues}} (and note that the NestJS arm is deliberately controller-level, no HTTP bootstrap). If the Express arm gains error mapping, re-run sandbox:token-budget so the full-src comparison reflects it.

area: packages/compiler + packages/cli (scanner correctness, affected narrowing, inspect artifact, verify argv, scaffold, determinism)
claim: Operations declared via object spread or computed string-literal keys inside a feature's operations literal are silently absent from the index (no diagnostic, no unresolved entry) while createApplication serves them at runtime. inspect/graph/affected are blind to these operations, duplicate-id detection skips them, and no test can ever associate with them. Non-static cases the scanner CAN see (helper-call ops, variable-held definitions) correctly emit metadata.static-operation-required + unresolved, so this is an inconsistent silent gap, not a policy.
repro: Fixture app1/src/features/alpha.ts: `const extraOps = { archive: command({...}) }; export const alpha = feature("alpha", { operations: { ...extraOps, create: command({...}), ["publish"]: command({...}), get: query({...}) satisfies unknown } })`. Then `node -e` with `analyzeProject({rootDir})` printed: diagnostics [], unresolved [], operations = [alpha.create, alpha.get, ...] — alpha.archive and alpha.publish missing. Runtime probe with `createApplication({features:[alpha],adapters:[NoteStorage.memory()]})`: app.call("alpha.publish") -> {ok:true,value:true}, app.call("alpha.archive") -> {ok:true,value:true}. Contrast probe: `made: makeOp()` and `feature("gadgets", definitionVariable)` DO produce diagnostics + unresolved entries.
suggestedFix: In the operations loop (scanner.ts:858-861) and the port-operations loop (scanner.ts:642), treat ts.isSpreadAssignment properties and computed property names (propertyName() === undefined for a real name node) the same as non-static operations: emit metadata.static-operation-required and push an unresolved entry so affected/verify widen conservatively.

area: packages/compiler + packages/cli (scanner correctness, affected narrowing, inspect artifact, verify argv, scaffold, determinism)
claim: The generated index is not machine-independent: every ordering comparator uses String.prototype.localeCompare with the environment's default locale, so identical sources yield different index bytes under different process locales — contradicting the 'byte-identical, machine-independent JSON' contract asserted at compiler.test.ts:174 and churning any committed/hashed .agentix/index.json across machines.
repro: Two features feature("zebra") and feature("ärenden"); generateIndex run in child processes with LC_ALL/LANG en_US.UTF-8 vs sv_SE.UTF-8 (Node v24.16.0). Output: `same-locale runs byte-identical: true`, `cross-locale runs byte-identical: false`; en_US feature order `ärenden , zebra`, sv_SE order `zebra , ärenden`; sha256 digests differ (4a9af621709b vs d6a5d1cfd60d).
suggestedFix: Replace the bare localeCompare comparators (scanner.ts:65, affected.ts:26, files.ts stableJson key sort at files.ts:138, context.ts:77) with a codepoint comparator (left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0) or a pinned Intl.Collator("en").

area: packages/compiler + packages/cli (scanner correctness, affected narrowing, inspect artifact, verify argv, scaffold, determinism)
claim: Narrow verification plans splice indexed test-file ids into the vitest argv unescaped; a legal marker-test file at the app root whose name starts with `--` is parsed by vitest as an option, not a filter. A file named `--shard.test.ts` flows into plan.tests and `agentix verify` then fails with a vitest startup TypeError (false-negative verification); other dash names silently mutate vitest config instead of filtering. area: packages/adapters-http
claim: handler.fetch and serveNode diverge for every core-legal null-body/informational success status (204/205/304/1xx): the fetch entry returns 500 INTERNAL while handle() and serveNode return the status. Core (descriptors.ts) and defineHttpRoute both accept 100..599, and DELETE+`http:{status:204}` is the canonical REST authoring, so a valid app 500s on one documented entry and succeeds on the other. Cause: toResponse() calls `new Response(body, {status})` with the non-empty envelope body, which undici rejects for null-body statuses (TypeError) and 1xx (RangeError); the outer catch converts it to 500 + onError. Side defects reproduced: (a) serveNode's 204/304 responses carry `content-length: 22` with zero body bytes (RFC 9110 forbids Content-Length on 204); (b) a 101 route makes serveNode responses crash undici clients (ERR_ASSERTION); (c) the onError fired from the fetch-entry catch passes info.path as the FULL URL ("http://x/notes/n1") with no operationId, unlike every other onError call site.
suggestedFix: Either (a) reject statuses the fixed JSON envelope cannot carry at compile time — tighten core http.status / per-error http / defineHttpRoute assertStatus to 200..599 excluding 204/205/304 — or (b) special-case them at emit time: in toResponse() use `new Response(null, {status})` (and in serveNode's writeOutcome skip the payload and content-length) for 204/205/304, and reject 1xx eagerly. Also make the fetch-entry catch pass url.pathname (and the matched operationId when available) in HttpErrorInfo.

area: packages/adapters-http
claim: The default input mapper silently discards syntactically valid non-object JSON bodies ([1,2], "str", 42, true, null) on object-schema routes: with an all-optional input schema (the typical PATCH partial-update shape) the request returns 200 and the operation executes with {} even though the client's entire payload was ignored — a silent data hazard. With required fields the client gets misleading 400 "Required field is missing" issues instead of "expected an object". Dispatching the same raw body directly would produce a correct INVALID_INPUT type error; the adapter's isPlainObjectBody guard in buildDefaultMapper erases the evidence. Identical on both entries, so entry-parity tests never catch it.
repro:
Probe: op `patch: command({input: s.object({title: s.optional(s.string({min:1})), count: s.optional(s.number())}), output: s.object({received: s.string()}), http:{method:"PATCH", path:"/opt"}, async execute({input}){return {received: JSON.stringify(input)};}})`; send PATCH /opt with each body via handler.fetch and via real HTTP against serveNode. Observed output:
  body=[1,2]        fetch: 200 {"ok":true,"value":{"received":"{}"}} | node: 200 {"ok":true,"value":{"received":"{}"}}
  body="a string"   fetch: 200 ... received "{}" | node: 200 ... received "{}"
  body=42 / true / null: same 200 with input {}.
Required-field variant (POST /notes body "[1,2]"): 400 INVALID_INPUT issues say required id/title missing — never mentions the body was not an object.
suggestedFix: In buildDefaultMapper (object-shape branch), when body !== undefined && !isPlainObjectBody(body), do not silently drop it: return the raw body as the input candidate (schema then rejects with a proper invalid-type issue), or short-circuit to the INVALID_INPUT envelope with an "expected a JSON object body" issue.

area: packages/adapters-http
claim: Wrong-method requests to a static route whose path arrives percent-encoded answer 404 NOT_FOUND instead of the documented 405 + Allow (P2_API_NOTES line 33 envelope table). The primary matcher has a decoded-segment second-chance static lookup, but the lazy-405 Allow computation (bucketMatches) only does a raw `staticRoutes.has(path)` — no decoded second chance. Any static route containing non-ASCII characters (e.g. "/café") ALWAYS arrives encoded over real HTTP (URL/undici percent-encode the request target), so wrong-method requests on such routes can never produce a 405. Both entries affected identically.
repro:
Probe: add op with http:{method:"POST", path:"/café"}; baseline PUT /notes correctly answers 405 allow=POST. Then:
  POST http://x/café (Request encodes to /caf%C3%A9) -> 200 {"ok":true,"value":{}}   // route reachable
  GET  http://x/café -> 404 allow: null {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND"}}    // expected 405 allow=POST
  serveNode POST /caf%C3%A9 -> 200 ; serveNode GET /caf%C3%A9 -> 404 allow: null
suggestedFix: In bucketMatches (router.ts ~line 399), mirror the primary path: when path contains "%", also try decodedStaticKey(segments) against bucket.staticRoutes before falling through to paramRoutes.

area: packages/adapters-http
claim: A streamed body that exceeds maxBodyBytes mid-stream (chunked, or CL-declared under the cap but streaming over it) leaves the connection in a not-idle/not-closed limbo: readRequestBody throws RequestBodyLimitError out of the `for await` loop, which destroys the IncomingMessage and stops Node from reading the socket — the client's FIN is never processed, closeIdleConnections() cannot reap the socket (not idle), and NodeHttpServer.close() blocks ~5.8s per such connection (Node keepAliveTimeout) instead of resolving immediately; concurrent occurrences accumulate (5 leaked sockets after 5 events, clients already gone). Contrast: the content-length fast-path 413 leaves the socket fully reusable (verified: 413 then pipelined request answered on same socket). Not a permanent leak, but graceful shutdown after any streamed 413 hangs multiple seconds; the 413/serveNode tests never stream past the cap so this is untested.
repro:
Probe (raw net.Socket against serveNode with maxBodyBytes:64): write "POST /notes HTTP/1.1..Transfer-Encoding: chunked" then three 40-byte chunks; server answers 413. Observed:
  v1 (client keeps socket open): close() HANG at 1s race; getConnections stays 1; full measurement: close() resolved after 5818ms.
  v2 (client destroys socket immediately): getConnections STILL 1 after destroy; close() resolved after 5715ms.
  v3: five such requests, all clients destroyed -> getConnections() == 5.
  Control (scenario e, 413 via declared content-length header, no streaming): close() resolved immediately; and 3b showed the same socket served a pipelined follow-up request (keep-alive preserved, no smuggling).
suggestedFix: After writing a 413 for a mid-stream overflow, explicitly release the socket: in handleRaw/writeOutcome, when `request.complete === false` and the outcome is 413, set `connection: close` and destroy the socket once the response flushes (e.g. `response.once("finish", () => response.destroy())`), or avoid destroying the stream by breaking out of the read loop and dumping the remainder instead of throwing through the async iterator.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: Production mode's documented "skip effect-output re-parse" silently changes DATA semantics, not just validation: in dev/test `effects.load()` hands execute a fresh parse copy, in production it hands back the adapter's LIVE object. A mutation of a loaded record inside execute therefore writes through to adapter/store state in production and is invisible in every test (tests run mode "test").
suggestedFix: Either (a) always detach effect outputs in production for built-in schemas (a cheap structural copy without re-validation), or (b) state explicitly in the mode matrix + AUTHORING.md that in production effect results ARE the adapter's objects and must be treated as read-only, and make dev/test match by returning the raw value there too (so tests exercise the same aliasing production has). Silent per-mode divergence in mutability is the part that must go.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: The documented `createApplication({ authorize })` hook is never consulted by the HTTP adapter's pre-body gate, which hard-codes the exported default subset check. An app whose hook GRANTS access (superuser/role bypass — the reason to pass a hook) gets 403 on every permissioned route over HTTP while app.dispatch succeeds, and core exposes no way to reach the effective gate (`"authorize" in app === false`).
suggestedFix: Expose the effective gate on the application (e.g. `readonly authorize(operation, principal?): boolean` on Application, defaulting to the exported authorize) and have adapters-http call `app.authorize(...)` for the pre-body 403 instead of the module-level default. Keeps 403-before-body-parse while making the hook the single source of truth.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: Schema issue accumulation is unbounded and uses spread-push: `(issues ??= []).push(...prefixIssues(key, result.issues))` (schema.ts:373, also 305/436) throws RangeError once a nested list exceeds ~125k issues, so a 244 KB request body (well under serveNode's 1 MiB default cap) turns an INVALID_INPUT rejection into an INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED fault → HTTP 500 instead of the specified 400; below that threshold the uncapped issue list amplifies a 195 KB request into a 9 MB 400 response (x46).
suggestedFix: (1) Replace every `push(...list)` in schema.ts (lines 305, 373, 436) with a bounded loop (`for (const i of list) issues.push(i)`) so a large failure list cannot blow the stack. (2) Cap accumulated issues per parse (e.g. stop at 100 and emit a truncation marker) — the cap also fixes the response amplification; the adapter can then serialize the whole list safely.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: Event emission deep-copies the payload a second time in production for no benefit: `event.payload.safeParse()` already returns a fully detached graph (verified: parse product shares no identity with the emitter's object), yet `snapshotStructuredValue` walks it again with `Object.defineProperty` per key. Measured cost is ~0.5 µs/item — a 100-line-item event adds 67.5 µs to a production dispatch, i.e. more than the entire 41–44 µs per-request HTTP budget the spec was tuned against, and 8.5x the validation it duplicates. No recorded benchmark emits any event (bench targets and benchmarks/runtime/src/benchmark.ts have no `emits`), so the "~0.16 µs, immaterial" event-path claim in SPEC §1 is unmeasured for non-trivial payloads.
suggestedFix: Skip snapshotStructuredValue entirely in production (parse products of built-in schemas are already fresh and unaliased — the only pass-through risk is a user-supplied custom Schema, which the code already treats as opaque), and in dev/test replace the defineProperty copy-walk with a pure deep-freeze walk over the parse product (no second graph). If a snapshot must stay for custom schemas, gate it on `parsed.data === payload` (identity) instead of always copying.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: `FAIL_RESULT` is an unregistered `Symbol("agentix.fail")` (descriptors.ts:49) while every other cross-boundary check in the framework is string-based (`descriptorType === "operation"`). With two copies of @agentix/core in one process (duplicated node_modules resolution, mismatched version pin between core and testing, non-deduped bundle) descriptors/adapters/app wiring all still work, but every `fail(...)` becomes unrecognizable to the other copy's dispatch and is silently reinterpreted as an output value → INVALID_OUTPUT fault (HTTP 500) instead of the declared 404/409. Success paths keep working, so the failure is invisible until an error path is hit.
suggestedFix: Use a realm/copy-stable brand: `export const FAIL_RESULT = Symbol.for("agentix.fail")` (keeps the non-enumerable, non-JSON-visible property while making identity cross-copy), or brand failures with a string key checked the same way descriptorType is. Add a test that loads two module instances and asserts a declared failure still completes.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: `createTestApplication` gives no way to reset the state of the fakes it auto-binds: `calls.reset()` clears only the recorded log (test-application.ts:229-239) while the Map-backed store fakes (test-application.ts:155-178) persist for the lifetime of the app object, so a module-scope test application plus a `beforeEach(() => calls.reset())` silently leaks records between tests (order-dependent failures like a spurious NOTE_ALREADY_EXISTS).
suggestedFix: Add a single `reset()` on the returned TestApplication that clears the fake stores, the call log, the clock and the id generator (and document that per-test construction is otherwise required). At minimum rename/scope `calls.reset()` so it cannot be mistaken for a state reset.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: `createTestApplication`'s structural store detection (test-application.ts:193, `STORE_OP_KINDS[opKey] === kind`) false-positives on any port that merely names an op get/save/delete/list with the matching kind: a non-store cache port's `read get` silently gets a Map-backed fake that always returns undefined instead of the loud "No test fake is derivable" stub, so the test exercises a permanently-missing dependency while its sibling ops still demand explicit overrides.
suggestedFix: Make store detection exact instead of heuristic: add a tiny non-generic marker on port.store-produced ops in core (e.g. `readonly preset: "store"` on PortOperationDescriptor, already requested in P2_API_NOTES coreChangeRequests) and key the memory fake on that marker; fall back to the loud throwing stub for every unmarked op.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: `ensures` checks receive the already-validated output object itself (application.ts:912, `ensure.check({ input, output: outcome.value })`) and only the outcome WRAPPER is frozen, so a check that mutates `output` injects undeclared fields into the response that no schema re-validates — and it happens in dev/test only, so the same operation returns different bodies per mode.
suggestedFix: Deep-freeze (or pass a frozen shallow proxy/copy of) the ensure context in dev/test so a postcondition cannot mutate a validated outcome — the freeze already claimed for "results/contexts" in dev/test does not currently protect the outcome value.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: An `emit` reached after dispatch settles throws its EVENT_OUTSIDE_EXECUTION guard into whatever context called it — from a timer/floating promise that is an uncaught exception that kills the process — while the symmetric case for effects is silently swallowed (the effect wrapper attaches `.then(remove, remove)`, application.ts:581-589). Fire-and-forget work inside execute therefore either crashes the server or vanishes, depending on which capability it touches.
suggestedFix: Make the closed-capability signal uniform and non-fatal after the dispatch has settled: once `lifecycle.active` is false and the result has been returned, route late emit/effect misuse to a per-application observer (or console.error in dev) instead of throwing into an arbitrary caller — or, if throwing is intended, apply it to effects too so the misuse is at least consistently visible.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: A custom `authorize` hook that throws makes `app.dispatch` REJECT its promise with the raw error instead of returning the documented 3-way result — the only user callback without fault containment (a throwing input schema yields INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED, a throwing execute yields EXECUTION_FAILED, a throwing ensure yields INVARIANT_VIOLATION).
suggestedFix: Wrap the authorizeHook call (application.ts:707-709) in try/catch and return a fault (e.g. a new AUTHORIZATION_FAILED code, or reuse EXECUTION_FAILED with the cause) so dispatch keeps its completed/rejected/fault contract for every user-supplied callback.

area: packages/core + packages/testing (v2 overhaul, git diff main...HEAD)
claim: `__proto__` is accepted as an identifier in two places where the assignment is silently swallowed instead of rejected: a feature operation key named `__proto__` (assigned via `operations[key] = ...`, descriptors.ts:860) disappears with no error at feature() or createApplication time even though the type system reports the id as dispatchable, and a declared object field named `__proto__` (schema.ts:372, `parsed[field.key] = result.data`) becomes the parse product's PROTOTYPE — the value survives property reads but is dropped from JSON, so a declared field silently vanishes from every HTTP response.
suggestedFix: Reject `__proto__` (and any key whose assignment would not create an own property) in assertOperationKey (descriptors.ts:901) and in `s.object()` shape validation, and build the maps with `Object.defineProperty`/null-prototype targets (schema.ts:361, descriptors.ts:851) so a declared key can never be swallowed.
